question: At the first shared query projection, do H4/D1 original-loss gradients locally move M5 mean logits upward, and do they help or hurt the M5 side loss?
reason: Retained M5/rest gradients aggregate H4/D1 with medium side and all activity losses; they cannot identify a D1 contribution. Prefix class marginals and the reconstructed-head remainder alone do not identify harmful transfer.

source_boundary.shared: All S/F output timeframes use this projection of128 hidden coordinates plus5 TF-one-hot columns plus1 query fraction. M5 has separate final side heads; other side/activity heads do not share M5-side bias parameters.

method: Original scalar loss supplies raw-logit derivative seeds. Eight disjoint loss VJPs and two all-row mean-M5-logit VJPs plus direct total give11autograd calls per intact batch. No loss reimplementation or optimizer.
required_parity: All original raw outputs/axes/masks/losses and both newly retained M5head inputs must match completed headcapture002 bitwise before each gradient measurement. Complete model/buffers/RNG/modes/identities/hooks unchanged and all parameter.grad None.
review_protocol: Recompute geometry from retained vectors; report both mean of within-batch dots and dot of mean vectors, all16/first3/other13 fixed groups. A negative mean-logit dot component-loss gradient predicts an infinitesimal ordinary-gradient increase in that logit, not an AdamW trajectory.
limitations: Initial frozen c171 and small dependent historical TRAIN panel only; not the full4096 training path or a generalization population.
Two shared projection tensors only; no general whole-model interference claim.
Class imbalance, gradient norm and mean-dot conflict alone do not authorize changing loss weights, removing features or training.
No candidate model, optimizer, later data, TEST, broker or trading authority.
